source_spans.locator: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance 18(3), published p.849, Abstract: target-identification plus probe-detection RSVP task; probe deficit from 180 to 450 ms; no deficit when a brief blank follows the target or when target identification is not required

Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance 18(3), published pp.853-855, Experiment 2: identify-target versus ignore-target control, fully specified X probe, significant detection deficit for +2 through +5 / 180-450 ms only when target identification is required

Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance 18(3), published pp.855-856, Experiment 3: blank inserted immediately after the target before the first posttarget letter; blanks of 90 ms or longer eliminate the deficit and reduce target-identification interference

Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance 18(3), published pp.856-858, Experiment 4: the same-duration blank moved to after the +1 item does not eliminate the deficit; immediate posttarget stimulation is required to initiate the suppressive process, which then persists despite later blank stimulation

Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance 18(3), published pp.858-860, General Discussion and proposed gate model: target-identification interference from an immediate novel item initiates transient suppression; once initiated it is described as ballistic; concluding empirical interval is 180-450 ms

provenance.venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance

conditions: rapid serial presentation of letters containing a partially specified white target and a fully specified X probe at variable posttarget positions
target identification is either required or explicitly omitted in a control condition
the timing of immediate posttarget visual input is manipulated by placing a blank either before the first posttarget letter or after that first posttarget letter
task: name the white target letter and report whether the X probe was present, or in the control condition ignore the white target and report only probe presence or absence
temporal_scope: probe detection is impaired primarily for probes presented about 180-450 ms after the target when target identification is required and immediate novel posttarget input occurs before identification is complete
a blank replacing the immediate +1 input prevents the deficit, whereas a similar blank inserted only after the +1 item does not

nodes.description: experimental requirement either to identify the partially specified white target or to ignore its defining color and omit target identification
novel first posttarget letter presented while target identification may still be incomplete
placement of a blank interval either immediately after the target before the first posttarget letter or later after that first posttarget letter
source-inferred confusion or interference produced when new posttarget input arrives before target identification is complete
source-proposed temporary suppression of subsequent visual input that is initiated when identification interference occurs
elapsed posttarget time or corresponding serial position at which the fully specified X probe is presented
percentage or probability of correctly reporting whether the fully specified X probe was present
rapid serial letter procedure comparing target-identification and ignore-target conditions while measuring X-probe detection over posttarget time and blank-placement manipulations
correct present-versus-absent judgment for the fully specified X probe

relations.description: probe detection shows a marked delay-dependent deficit from about 180 to 450 ms when target identification is required, but not when the target-defining color is ignored
the source infers identification interference when novel +1 input arrives before target identification is complete; replacing that immediate input with a blank relieves the interference
the source's proposed mechanism uses interference during target identification to initiate a temporary suppressive state rather than positing a generic depleted processing budget
once the proposed suppressive state is initiated, detection of later probes is reduced for a limited posttarget interval
a blank that replaces the immediate +1 input prevents the deficit, whereas a comparable blank inserted only after the +1 item leaves the deficit intact
in the proposed sequence, interference during unfinished target identification occurs before initiation of the transient suppressive state
the RSVP procedure measures the posttarget time course of the detection deficit under target-task and blank-placement manipulations
probe performance is scored by correct present-versus-absent judgments
